chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Muhammad bin Isa bin Ubayd, from Ibn Abi Umayr, who said:
Isa bin Ayn, when he performed Hajj, would turn to supplication for his brethren when he arrived at the Station (Mawqif), until the people departed.

I said to him, 'You spend your wealth and exhaust your body, and when you come to the place where needs are presented to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, you turn to supplicating for your brethren and neglect yourself?'
He said, 'I am relying upon the supplication of the Angels for me, and am in doubt regarding the supplication for myself.'

key_terms.الْمَوْقِف: The Station (Mawqif), specifically referring to the place of standing during Hajj, such as Arafat
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic (an honorific for Allah)

ai.seo_question: Why did Isa bin Ayn prefer to supplicate for others during Hajj instead of for himself?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual humility of Isa bin Ayn, who preferred the intercession of angels over his own supplication at the Mawqif, reflecting a deep sense of unworthiness. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the efficacy of communal prayer and the merit of prioritizing others' needs during the pivotal moments of Hajj. It serves as a practical model for believers to cultivate reliance on divine mercy through the agency of the faithful and the angels.
